A1.justification: Both PDFs describe C-FREE and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Renamed variants and relocated experiments can be matched reliably despite substantial formatting changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original MoleculeNet, Kraken, Drugs-75K, and EXP experiments, including ablations, learning curves, and subgraph-generation timings.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds QM9 and ZINC evaluations, encoder variants, and additional ablation and structural-analysis results.

M1.justification: v2 adds PaiNN as an alternative to SchNet and tests Murcko-scaffold partitions instead of EgoNets. These are localized encoder and view-generation variants; the complementary-subgraph prediction objective, EMA teacher, transformer fusion, and downstream aggregation procedures remain. Renaming LIN/DS to MOL/SUB does not change the method.

E1.justification: v2 adds QM9 evaluation across six reported property groups, including Mu, alpha, HOMO/LUMO/gap, R2, Cv, and ZPVE, plus ZINC property prediction. GEOM, MoleculeNet, Kraken, Drugs-75K, and EXP remain; the relocated Kraken and EXP experiments are not new coverage.

E2.justification: MoleculeNet fine-tuning gains MolFM, GEM, and UniMol comparators, while the frozen-backbone comparison gains GraphMVP in v2 Table 15. QM9 introduces comparisons with UniMol2 sizes and randomly initialized PaiNN. JOAO and GPT-GNN remain in the appendix; the METIS timing comparison is removed.

E3.justification: v2 introduces single-versus-three-conformer configurations, QM9 encoder and partitioning comparisons, and EMA/radius experiments pretrained on Drugs-75K using one EgoNet per molecule. It also analyzes subgraphs from 200 sampled GEOM molecules. The original MoleculeNet scaffold-split protocol and main training budget remain.

E4.justification: New analyses test EMA schedules, EgoNet radius, separator tokens, Murcko partitioning, and encoder/conformer choices; Appendix A.10 measures subgraph structure and coverage. Original modality, predictor, and EXP analyses remain. Conversely, v1 Appendix A.3's empirical EgoNet-versus-METIS runtime analysis is removed.

E5.justification: The reported three scaffold splits, three-run experiments, and mean/standard-deviation learning curves remain. Added tables continue the existing uncertainty-reporting style. The separator-token discussion asserts statistical insignificance but documents no new significance test, confidence interval, seed policy, or repeated-run count.

E6.justification: Original results are largely retained: the SchNet three-conformer MoleculeNet average remains 77.50. The new PaiNN variant reports 79.81 under a different encoder configuration. QM9, ablation, and ZINC results are added; ZINC reports 0.204±0.015 for C-FREE versus 0.434±0.014 for GraphJEPA. The original runtime results are removed.

T1.justification: The invariance lemma and ESAN/1-WL expressiveness argument remain substantively unchanged. However, v2 removes v1 Appendix A.3's asymptotic derivation comparing approximately linear EgoNet extraction with the stated METIS logarithmic overhead. This removes a secondary theoretical analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract and four introductory contributions retain their essential claims. The conclusion extends the claimed state-of-the-art regression coverage to QM9 and adds the EMA scheduler alongside the predictor as critical to avoiding collapse.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations concerning EMA dynamics, context/target size balance, separator tokens as possible attention sinks, and chemically informed partitions. It also discusses SMILES exclusion, acknowledges Drugs-75K/pretraining overlap, and suggests failed conformer generation and dummy coordinates explain weak SIDER performance.

D1.justification: v2 specifies boundary-node duplication and edge assignment, supplies PaiNN configuration information, and discloses dummy-coordinate handling for failed conformers. It removes the named PyTorch Geometric extraction helper and explicit checkpoint-availability statement. The code link and most hyperparameters remain; checkpoint withdrawal cannot be inferred.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning against molecular foundation models, discussing ChemBERTa, SCAGE, UniMol/UniMol2, MolFM, and GEM, including differences in pretraining scale. Appendix A.14 also contextualizes 'contrast-free' terminology. The original three-category related-work organization and central novelty claim remain.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative and appendix organization are substantially revised: Kraken probing and EXP move into dedicated appendix sections, additional analyses receive separate subsections, and LIN/DS terminology becomes MOL/SUB. Predictor-input wording is clarified. The reproducibility and LLM statements disappear, while acknowledgements and an impact statement are added.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column main-text layout, redraws Figure 1 with explicit token flow, and adds downstream-pipeline and EMA figures. Original Kraken probe plots are consolidated into Figure 6, and predictor plots are vertically rearranged. Tables are expanded, added, and relocated; the runtime table disappears.

improvement.justification: Stronger baselines, encoder/conformer comparisons, and new ablations improve the empirical assessment beyond v1's narrower comparisons. The gains are tempered by removal of direct runtime evidence and new reporting inconsistencies: v2 Table 7 reports 0.491 for k=1 although its displayed task scores average 0.502, and the QM9 discussion incorrectly gives 3D-only models an advantage on HOMO/LUMO/gap. Overall, the evidence is more informative, but these reliability issues limit the improvement.
